character: a tired young man with messy dark hair, grey hoodie

scenes.narration: This is what happens to your body if you stay awake for *eleven* days.
scenes.visual: close-up of {character} staring at a glowing phone in a dark bedroom at night, wide bloodshot eyes
scenes.action: the tired man's eyes twitch and widen as the phone light flickers on his face, slow push in

scenes.narration: After just one night, your reaction time *drops* like you've had a few drinks.
scenes.visual: {character} slumped at an office desk, coffee cups piled up, blurry computer screen

scenes.narration: By day three, your brain starts taking tiny naps without asking you. They're called *microsleeps*.
scenes.visual: inside a glowing cartoon human brain, small sections switching off like light bulbs

scenes.narration: By day five, you can start seeing and hearing things that aren't there.
scenes.visual: {character} in a dim hallway, strange shadow figures on the walls, eerie blue light

scenes.narration: In 1964, a teenager named Randy Gardner made it to eleven days. Scientists watched him the whole time.
scenes.visual: retro 1960s science lab, scientists in white coats with clipboards watching a tired teenager

scenes.narration: And after all that? He slept fourteen hours and woke up fine. So the next time you scroll at 3 AM, remember what happens to your body if you stay awake for eleven days.
scenes.visual: {character} finally asleep in a cosy bed, warm morning sunlight through the window
